finding: The system relies on the assumption that frontline staff will consistently self-report machine failures that jeopardize their own operational throughput, creating a high-incentive environment for them to hide status changes and "pencil-whip" the documentation.

The system prioritizes mathematical occupancy over physical reality, creating a high probability of "no-show" conflicts and customer churn caused by aggressive, automated, and error-prone scheduling policies.

The system imposes a rigid physical limit on order volume and assumes perfect inventory accuracy, ensuring that any deviation—from mis-shelved books to staff interruptions—collapses the workflow into a chaotic and error-prone "hunt-and-search" cycle.
The system imposes an unrealistic administrative burden on exhausted closing staff that will lead to either systemic non-compliance or the falsification of safety logs to expedite clock-out times.

The system relies on a high-trust, high-tech interface in a low-trust, high-interference physical environment, creating an inventory and loss-prevention nightmare that shifts the labor burden from the counter to an unsustainable cycle of manual intervention and server-side timeouts.

The solution attempts to replicate a frictionless "Apple Store" experience in a high-friction, industrial environment where the physical weight and size of products render mobile bagging and ad-hoc security de-tagging ergonomically impossible and a high-risk security liability.

The system decentralizes diagnostic authority to anonymous customers, creating an easily exploitable vector for service disruption and a high-friction administrative burden that staff will inevitably bypass during peak hours.

The system imposes a high-maintenance manual labor tax on the business owner that will be abandoned during peak hours, and replaces revenue loss with a combination of margin-eroding discounts and avoidable customer churn.

The solution imposes an unsustainable, high-expertise manual labor requirement that will be abandoned by frontline staff during peak periods, resulting in a degraded customer experience and fragmented, un-sellable inventory.
The protocol imposes an unrealistic administrative and technical burden on frontline staff, ensuring the monitoring system will be falsified or abandoned as soon as operational pressure mounts.

The system decentralizes the responsibility for inventory to a "universal pool" while simultaneously imposing a high-tech tracking requirement that lacks a reliable, fraud-proof way to attribute lost items to specific individuals, ensuring a rapid depletion of assets and a failure of the accountability loop.

The system relies on a non-secure physical token that provides no actual deterrent to theft and creates an unmanageable logistical nightmare for staff when the "gravity-fed" racks inevitably jam due to student non-compliance.

The system eliminates all barriers to inventory removal while simultaneously relying on a complex, high-maintenance, and easily bypassed "reward" loop, ensuring rapid asset depletion and operational failure.

The system attempts to manage physical inventory through a digital ID-tracking loop that lacks a physical confirmation of return, ensuring that assets will be discarded or stolen with no ability for the business to audit or enforce accountability.

The system attempts to enforce digital accountability in a high-volume, low-security physical environment where the impossibility of verifying individual returns will lead to systemic inventory loss and a collapse of user trust through inaccurate automated charges.

The solution imposes a high-complexity technical administrative burden on low-skill staff, ensuring the system will be permanently bypassed or disabled the moment it experiences a mechanical or calibration fault.
The model replaces a managed labor bottleneck with an unmonitored, high-risk self-service environment that invites food tampering, inventory theft, and rapid product degradation.

The system assumes universal customer compliance and high-skill staff multitasking, creating a fragile operational loop that will collapse into social friction and total service paralysis the moment a customer refuses to follow the digital-only protocol.
The system relies on a high-bandwidth, error-prone verbal communication loop that will be rendered inaudible and secondary the moment the POS operator becomes overwhelmed by transaction volume.

The system assumes a frictionless, high-compliance environment where customers follow floor markings and technology never fails, ignoring the inevitable social friction and operational paralysis that occur when digital syncs lag or demand surges.

The system relies on inherently imprecise network-based occupancy tracking that is easily gamed by students while simultaneously creating a high-liability, labor-intensive property management mandate for library staff.

The solution relies on a "Flex" staffing model that is guaranteed to evaporate during volume surges, turning the PIT desk into an unstaffed bottleneck that creates dangerous, high-liability gaps in patient care.

The solution attempts to engineer social spontaneity through fragile, temporary funding and invasive digital monitoring, ensuring the project collapses into expensive urban blight once the pilot program’s budget expires.

The system replaces automated technical gates with a resource-intensive pairing requirement that will inevitably become a labor bottleneck, ultimately leading teams to bypass the planning sessions entirely under deadline pressure.
The solution creates an administrative "paperwork tax" that will be ignored or actively subverted the moment production demands conflict with energy-saving protocols.
